headlines.title: Unusual Options Activity: LEAPS Offer Low-Cost Rebound Bets on 2 Beaten-Down Consumer Stocks
headlines.summary: Yesterday’s unusual options activity flagged Diageo’s Jan. 2028 $40 call and McDonald’s Jan. 2029 $250 call as contrarian rebound plays. Diageo’s deep in-the-money call needs just a 2.14% gain to break even, making it the better risk/reward proposition.

headlines.title: Is UBER Stock Worth Betting on Now, Riding on Its Expansion Drive?
headlines.summary: Uber's $2.3 billion ezCater deal, robotaxi partnerships and other diversification efforts bolster its growth prospects, but weak stock performance raises questions for investors.

headlines.title: Did Uber Technologies' Fall Catch You Out? What Investors Missed
headlines.summary: If you had decided on 21 October 2025 that Uber Technologies was too complicated or too aggressive on autonomous vehicles and global delivery deals, sitting it out might feel like a relief today. For Uber Technologies shareholders, the loss over the past year was 26.7%, including dividends. The question is not who guessed right. It is which assumptions about AV spending, consolidation deals, and regulatory risk were already on the table when that choice was made.

headlines.title: Taiwan blocks Grab’s $600 million Foodpanda deal, citing Uber’s 13.1% stake in the Southeast Asian super app
headlines.summary: The decision, for now, ends Grab's first attempt to expand outside Southeast Asia.

headlines.title: Uber Offers Drivers Hundreds of Dollars in Extra Cash. Here’s What They Have to Do to Get It.
headlines.summary: As the busy holiday season approaches, some drivers are seeing big bonus offers, a perk many haven’t encountered in years.

description: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. The Mobility segment connects consumers with a range of transportation modalities, such as ridesharing, carsharing, micromobility, rentals, public transit, taxis, and other modalities; and offers riders in a variety of vehicle types, as well as financial partnerships products and advertising services. The Delivery segment allows consumers to search for and discover restaurants to grocery, alcohol, convenience, and other retailers, as well as order a meal or other items, and either pick-up at the restaurant or have it delivered; and provides Uber direct, a white-label delivery-as-a-service for retailers and restaurants, as well as advertising services. The Freight segment manages transportation and logistics networks, which connects shippers and carriers in digital marketplace, including carriers upfronts, pricing, and shipment booking; and offers on-demand platform to automate logistics end-to-end transactions for small-and medium-sized businesses to global enterprises. Uber Technologies, Inc. has strategic partnership with Mews to embed ride booking, real-time tracking and integrated billing directly into the Mews platform. The company was formerly known as Ubercab, Inc. and changed its name to Uber Technologies, Inc. in February 2011. Uber Technologies, Inc. was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
